status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The reported interruption is unwanted operational behaviour directly engaging repair. The Times of India quotes the provider identifying login-focused errors and reporting resolution; Tom's Guide corroborates a roughly thirty-minute disruption followed by substantial recovery. The disclosed restoration is affirmative evidence of repair for this recovery stage; no taxonomy success, internal root cause or universal individual recovery is inferred.

conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence is a bounded access interruption whose operative state remained legible as login failure. The evidence does not show that account validity, entitlement, restriction or verification state was misrepresented, nor that an authentication transition failed to propagate. The governance requirement is accurate component and recovery disclosure; the current taxonomy does not classify ordinary login unavailability without an additional mechanism. Both clauses retain resolved-no-mapping dispositions. Accurate login-focused reporting is not proof of every access-state success-recognition condition, while login failure alone does not establish any of the rejected failure mechanisms. The record remains fully adjudicated and unclassified. No eligible FC-derived or independently source-identified admitted external requirement is established; this absence does not establish compliance.
